selection_reasoning: This task is a single atomic action that is clearly observable and verifiable in the Minecraft environment. The player needs to use a hoe on a dirt block to convert it into farmland. It requires minimal deep Minecraft knowledge (just knowing to use a hoe on dirt), is easily set up in a scene (dirt block + hoe in inventory), and the result is clearly verifiable (the block type changes from dirt to farmland). Since we are selecting exactly 1 task, there are no dependency edges needed.

milestones.description: Uses count_in_box_at_least(kind='block', object='farmland', min_count=1) because tilling dirt with a hoe converts the dirt block into a farmland block in-place. We check for at least one farmland block within a generous box (±5 XZ, Y from -2 to 0) around spawn, which fully covers the 9x9 dirt platform placed at Y=-1 relative to spawn. This rule type is preferred for place/build/transform tasks where a block state change is the observable outcome.

scene_description: A flat 9x9 dirt platform with cleared air above, a water source block for hydration, and a stone foundation below. The player spawns with a diamond hoe equipped, ready to till any dirt block into farmland by right-clicking (using) the hoe on dirt.
task_text: Use the diamond hoe in your inventory to till a dirt block into farmland. Right-click (use) the hoe while aiming at any dirt block on the ground.
atomic_tasks_ordered: till dirt into farmland with hoe
design_notes: The player spawns on a 9x9 dirt platform. The diamond hoe is given directly to inventory (slot 0, equipped). The air fill clears 6 blocks above the dirt to remove tree leaves/logs. A water source is placed at the far edge for farmland hydration realism. Stone below prevents accidental mining through. The task requires the player to select the hoe, aim at a dirt block, and right-click (use) to convert it to farmland. Any single dirt block converted counts as success.
